newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-198 DETAINED AROUND DORTMUND V UNITED TIE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-198 DETAINED AROUND DORTMUND V UNITED TIE.

text.p: German police detained 198 people for public order offences surrounding Wednesday's European Cup semifinal between Borussia Dortmund and Manchester United.
A police spokesman said around 120 of those detained were Germans and none of the offences was serious.
Manchester fans were involved in trouble at the club's last away tie in Portugal. Eight English fans were injured after a clash with riot police following the quarter-final at Porto.

"The expectations were hyped up in view of what happened at Porto but things haven't turned out as people feared," the spokesman said. "We've already released the first of the English people we detained."
The police said the offences were comparable to those that they would have to deal with at a domestic league game.
They hailed the relatively peaceful nature of events as a victory for their policy of trying to create a friendly atmosphere between home supporters and away fans.
Around 1,500 fans enjoyed a pre-match party in the city centre.

The police, mounting their biggest-ever security operation for a Dortmund match, kept their presence discreet while fans of the two teams drank beer, sang and danced together in sunshine at the party laid on by Borussia Dortmund and city authorities.
"This is wonderful," Borussia spokesman Josef Schneck said. "The mood is as good as the weather."
Police believed some troublemakers had travelled from other parts of Germany for the match. The spokesman said the hooligans were well-known and were being closely monitored.
Around 4,000 English fans were expected in Dortmund for the sell-out match, about 500 of them without tickets.
The mood in the city appeared relaxed, with police donning the scarves of the two clubs, distributing souvenir stickers to fans and even taking photographs for them.
The fans were entertained by music and guest appearances by former Dortmund and Manchester United players.
"I hope when these people come back to Manchester you look after them," former United stalwart Pat Crerand told the Manchester fans from the temporary stage erected for the party.
Beer stalls scattered around the city centre square where the party was being held did a heavy trade, serving up some of Dortmund's best-known brews to thirsty fans.
